title: Surjectivity descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $0\in I$ and let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of schemes over $S_0$, where $S_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the base change of $f_0$ to $S_i$ and $f:X\to Y$ its base change to $S$ (fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]). If $f$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is surjective for some $i\ge0$ (Stacks Limits, Lemma 07RR).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, line 2069), in Situation Tag 081D (situation-descent-property, line 1739); its proof: $f_0$ is of finite presentation, so $E=f_0(X_0)$ is constructible (Chevalley, Morphisms Lemma Tag 054J); the image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$; $Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$, so Limits Lemma Tag 05F4 (lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible) gives $i$ with $Y_i\to Y_0$ mapping into $E$

proof.text: Because $X_0$ and $Y_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the locally finitely presented morphism $f_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence of finite presentation in the sense used by Chevalley's theorem.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR, first sentence ('$f_0$ is of finite presentation') together with Morphisms Definition Tag 01TP

proof.text: The image $E=f_0(X_0)\subseteq Y_0$ is constructible by Chevalley's theorem for a morphism of finite presentation between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR, proof; Morphisms Lemma Tag 054J

proof.text: For every $i\ge0$, the image of the base change $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ under $Y_i\to Y_0$: a point of $Y_i$ lies in that inverse image exactly when its pullback to $Y_i\times_{Y_0}X_0=X_i$ lies over a point of $X_0$. The same identification holds at the limit, so the image of $f:X\to Y$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR, proof; sentence 'The image of $f_i$ is the inverse image of $E$ in $Y_i$'

proof.text: Surjectivity of $f$ says that the projection $Y\to Y_0$ has image contained in $E$, by the image identification in the preceding step.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR, proof; sentence '$Y\to Y_0$ maps into $E$'

proof.text: Apply the finite-stage containment lemma to $E\subseteq Y_0$. It gives $i\ge0$ such that the image of $Y_i\to Y_0$ is contained in $E$. By the image identification, $f_i$ is then surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RR, proof; Limits Lemma Tag 05F4

surjective morphism at the limit of an inverse system of schemes implies surjective at a finite stage (constructible image)
